To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a framework AMOS that trains a text encoder as a discriminator to distinguish replaced tokens generated by multiple masked language models, and we show that this method outperforms ELECTRAs and recent state-of-art pretrained models by 1 point on GLUE.
we propose a novel framework for pretraining text encoders that outperforms the state-of-the-art by about 1 GLUE point.
AMOS is a new framework that pretrains the encoder with an adversarial learning curriculum via multiple auxiliary generators and outperforms ELECTRABERT base on the GLUE benchmarks by about 1point.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (a) how to train multiple MLMs jointly for better pretraining, (b) how to learn the mixture weights over the MLMs' outputs for better adversarial learning, (c) how to assemble multiple MLM models for better efficiency, and (d) how to improve pretraining by combining multiple MLMs with different sizes and learning the mixture weights.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper presents an interesting idea of using adversarial learning for pretraining text encoders.
AMOS outperformed all previous methods in the literature.
our proposed framework AMOS is an effective way to train BERT-style models with an Adversarially learned Mixture of Signals from multiple auxiliary MLMs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a new framework for pretraining text encoders, which is simple and efficient.
we propose a new adversarial learning framework for training text encoders with a mixture of training signals.
adversarial learning is a powerful tool for pretraining text encoders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a mixture of training signals from multiple generators can be more powerful than one generator.
adversarial learning can benefit from a curriculum of training signals from multiple auxiliary generators of different difficulty.
adversarial pretraining with multiple MLMs can provide a better training signal for the discriminator, and that a mixture of training signals is more effective than a single training signal.
